skill.name: dependency-auditor
skill.description: Audit project dependencies for vulnerabilities, outdated packages, license concerns, and supply chain risks.
skill.summary: Find dependency security risks and plan safe remediation steps.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, sample report sections, and placeholder URLs in SKILL.md. The skill has no bundled executable code and no prompt injection evidence, but it recommends dependency-changing commands and third-party scanning without explicit consent guardrails.

remediation.issue: Dependency-changing examples lack explicit confirmation guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to ask before install, update, audit fix, prune, uninstall, or hook changes. Prefer read-only audits first.

remediation.issue: Third-party scanner commands may share dependency metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add a notice before Snyk or similar commands. Require user approval and approved accounts before external monitoring.

remediation.issue: Example commands mix reporting guidance and execution steps.
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as recommendations unless the user asks to run them. Include verification and rollback steps.

semantic_findings.title: Dependency-Changing Commands Need Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends audit fix, install, update, uninstall, and prune commands without a clear instruction to request user approval before changes. These actions can modify manifests, lockfiles, hooks, or installed packages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited blocks contain commands that can change project dependencies or local state. The file frames them as remediation steps but does not add an explicit confirmation requirement.

content.value_statement: Dependency vulnerabilities create release risk and supply chain exposure. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code review packages and plan fixes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews dependency manifests for known vulnerabilities, outdated packages, license issues, and suspicious packages.
Maps direct and transitive dependency risks into critical, high, medium, and low priorities.
Suggests safer versions, replacement packages, migration notes, and verification steps.
Covers npm, Python, Go, Ruby, Maven, and .NET audit workflows.
Provides report formats with executive summaries, remediation phases, and monitoring recommendations.
limitations: Results depend on current advisory databases and installed audit tools.
Some examples require package manager access, network access, or third-party scanner accounts.
It cannot prove a fix is safe without tests and project context.
License guidance is informational and does not replace legal review.

use_cases.title: Triage Release Risk
use_cases.description: Review dependency vulnerabilities before a release and identify fixes that need urgent approval.

use_cases.title: Prepare Upgrade Plan
use_cases.description: Compare vulnerable packages, fixed versions, and likely migration work before changing dependencies.

use_cases.title: Improve Supply Chain Controls
use_cases.description: Create CI audit, advisory monitoring, and dependency review practices for a repository.

prompt_templates.title: Audit One Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this project for dependency vulnerabilities. Start with package manifests, summarize severe issues, and list safe next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Transitive Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze direct and transitive dependency risks. Highlight the parent packages that introduce vulnerable transitive packages.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased remediation plan. Separate read-only checks, dependency changes, testing, and rollout verification.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI Dependency Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a dependency security workflow for CI. Include severity thresholds, exception handling, license checks, and monitoring ownership.

output_examples.input: A Node.js project has vulnerable lodash and outdated express dependencies.
output: Critical lodash issue requires immediate update to a fixed version.
Express ecosystem updates should be tested in staging before release.
Run tests after dependency changes and document any exceptions.

output_examples.input: A team wants weekly dependency monitoring across services.
output_examples.output: Recommended output: a CI audit plan with severity thresholds, Dependabot ownership, license review, and a response schedule.

output_examples.input: A Python service uses old requirements and has no lockfile.
output: Add a reproducible lockfile process before broad upgrades.
Run advisory checks for direct and transitive packages.
Prioritize fixes that have active exploits or public patches.

best_practices: Start with read-only audit commands before applying dependency changes.
Review lockfile changes, release notes, and tests before merging upgrades.
Document accepted vulnerability and license exceptions with owners and expiry dates.
anti_patterns: Running automatic fixes on production branches without review.
Ignoring transitive dependency paths when only parent packages can be changed.
Treating scanner output as final without checking exploitability and project usage.

faq.question: Does this skill install packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides audit steps and remediation guidance. Confirm any install, update, or uninstall command before running it.

faq.question: Which ecosystems does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers npm, Python, Go, Ruby, Maven, and .NET workflows described in the skill.

faq.question: Can it find transitive vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes dependency tree review and parent package remediation guidance.

faq.question: Does it replace a commercial scanner?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret scanner results and plan fixes. Current vulnerability databases are still required.

faq.question: Can it handle license risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes license summaries and flags restrictive licenses for human review.

faq.question: Is third-party scanning required?
faq.answer: No. The skill mentions tools such as Snyk, but teams can use local or approved scanners.
